correctness.rationale: For operator Schmidt rank k, the elementary tensor expansion gives SR(Uv)<=kp. The involution property gives the reverse p<=kq. For q<=p the disjoint-index controlled transposition construction has exactly q orthogonal nonzero Schmidt terms. For q>p the frame-extension lemma constructs q orthonormal control vectors whose normalized group sums equal the input Schmidt basis, while disjoint second-factor swaps create exactly q nonzero output terms. Orthogonal controls and order-two blocks give U*=U and U²=I. This proves the lower bound is sharp for all m,n,p,q; the 254 finite test cases corroborate but do not prove it.

value.rationale: Self-adjoint order-two gates are a natural and much smaller reversible gate class than arbitrary unitaries. The theorem proves an exact and coefficient-independent equivalence of the optimal Schmidt-rank transition costs in both classes in all finite dimensions; the increasing-rank construction requires a genuinely different orthogonal-frame alignment from the motivating unrestricted proof. It is a complete structural classification, not a renamed existing unrestricted formula.
